next-env.d.ts
# Idea Log

Log ideas, score them on differentiation, evidence, cost, and reversibility
(1-5 each), and see them ranked by total score. When an idea finishes or gets
abandoned, record what actually happened and re-score it in hindsight to see
where your predictions were off.

- Full TypeScript stack: Next.js App Router + API routes, Prisma, PostgreSQL.
- Accounts with private ideas (cookie session, `bcrypt` password hashing).
- Share a single idea by unshareable/unguessable link — no signup required to view.
- Score ranges enforced both in the API (Zod) and the database (CHECK constraints).

## Stack

- **Framework**: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript
- **API**: Next.js Route Handlers under `src/app/api/**`
- **Database**: PostgreSQL via Prisma ORM
- **Auth**: Signed JWT session cookie (`jose`), `bcryptjs` for password hashing — no third-party auth service
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4, hand-rolled UI kit (`src/components/ui.tsx`)

## Getting started

Requires Docker (for local Postgres) and Node 20+.

```bash
pnpm install          # also runs `prisma generate`
cp .env.example .env  # fill in DATABASE_URL / JWT_SECRET (or keep the defaults)
pnpm db:up            # starts Postgres in Docker
pnpm db:migrate       # applies migrations
pnpm dev              # http://localhost:3000
```

## Data model

- `User` — email, password hash, name.
- `Idea` — belongs to a user. Prediction scores (`differentiation`, `evidence`,
  `cost`, `reversibility`, each 1-5) are required at creation. `status` is
  `ACTIVE` / `DONE` / `ABANDONED`. Once an idea is finished or abandoned, an
  `outcome` (free text) and a second set of hindsight scores (`hDifferentiation`
  etc.) can be recorded. `shareToken` is a unique nullable string — set when
  the owner turns on link sharing, cleared when revoked.

Total score and hindsight delta are computed on read (`src/lib/scoring.ts`),
not stored, so they're always consistent with the underlying scores.

## Key routes

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/`, `/login`, `/register` | Public marketing + auth |
| `/ideas` | Private dashboard, ranked by total score, with a calibration summary |
| `/ideas/[id]` | Edit an idea, record its outcome, manage its share link |
| `/s/[token]` | Public, read-only view of a single shared idea — no auth |

All `/ideas*` pages are protected by `src/proxy.ts` (Next's middleware
convention) in addition to per-request auth checks in each Server Component
and API route, so there's no route that only "looks" protected client-side.

## Notes

- Prisma is pinned to the 6.x line rather than the newly-released 7, which
  requires driver adapters and a separate `prisma.config.ts` — not worth the
  churn for a project this size.
- `docker-compose.yml` runs Postgres only; the app itself runs with `pnpm dev`
  / `pnpm build && pnpm start`.
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: idealog
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: idealog
      POSTGRES_DB: idealog
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - idealog_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  idealog_pgdata:
import type { NextConfig } from "next";

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  /* config options here */
};

export default nextConfig;
ignoredBuiltDependencies:
  - sharp
  - unrs-resolver
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum IdeaStatus {
  ACTIVE
  DONE
  ABANDONED
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  email        String   @unique
  passwordHash String
  name         String?
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())

  ideas Idea[]
}

model Idea {
  id     String @id @default(cuid())
  userId String
  user   User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  title       String
  description String     @default("")
  status      IdeaStatus @default(ACTIVE)

  // Prediction scores, each 1-5, recorded when the idea is logged.
  differentiation Int
  evidence        Int
  cost            Int
  reversibility   Int

  // Hindsight: filled in once the idea is finished or abandoned.
  outcome            String?
  outcomeRecordedAt  DateTime?
  hDifferentiation   Int?
  hEvidence          Int?
  hCost              Int?
  hReversibility     Int?

  // Set when the idea is shared publicly via link; null = not shared.
  shareToken String? @unique

  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  @@index([userId])
  @@index([userId, status])
}
-- CreateEnum
CREATE TYPE "IdeaStatus" AS ENUM ('ACTIVE', 'DONE', 'ABANDONED');

-- CreateTable
CREATE TABLE "User" (
    "id" TEXT NOT NULL,
    "email" TEXT NOT NULL,
    "passwordHash" TEXT NOT NULL,
    "name" TEXT,
    "createdAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    CONSTRAINT "User_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);

-- CreateTable
CREATE TABLE "Idea" (
    "id" TEXT NOT NULL,
    "userId" TEXT NOT NULL,
    "title" TEXT NOT NULL,
    "description" TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    "status" "IdeaStatus" NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE',
    "differentiation" INTEGER NOT NULL,
    "evidence" INTEGER NOT NULL,
    "cost" INTEGER NOT NULL,
    "reversibility" INTEGER NOT NULL,
    "outcome" TEXT,
    "outcomeRecordedAt" TIMESTAMP(3),
    "hDifferentiation" INTEGER,
    "hEvidence" INTEGER,
    "hCost" INTEGER,
    "hReversibility" INTEGER,
    "shareToken" TEXT,
    "createdAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL,

    CONSTRAINT "Idea_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);

-- CreateIndex
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "User_email_key" ON "User"("email");

-- CreateIndex
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "Idea_shareToken_key" ON "Idea"("shareToken");

-- CreateIndex
CREATE INDEX "Idea_userId_idx" ON "Idea"("userId");

-- CreateIndex
CREATE INDEX "Idea_userId_status_idx" ON "Idea"("userId", "status");

-- AddForeignKey
ALTER TABLE "Idea" ADD CONSTRAINT "Idea_userId_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("userId") REFERENCES "User"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;
-- Enforce 1-5 range on prediction scores and hindsight scores at the database level.
ALTER TABLE "Idea"
  ADD CONSTRAINT "Idea_differentiation_range" CHECK ("differentiation" BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  ADD CONSTRAINT "Idea_evidence_range" CHECK ("evidence" BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  ADD CONSTRAINT "Idea_cost_range" CHECK ("cost" BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  ADD CONSTRAINT "Idea_reversibility_range" CHECK ("reversibility" BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  ADD CONSTRAINT "Idea_hDifferentiation_range" CHECK ("hDifferentiation" IS NULL OR "hDifferentiation" BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  ADD CONSTRAINT "Idea_hEvidence_range" CHECK ("hEvidence" IS NULL OR "hEvidence" BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  ADD CONSTRAINT "Idea_hCost_range" CHECK ("hCost" IS NULL OR "hCost" BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  ADD CONSTRAINT "Idea_hReversibility_range" CHECK ("hReversibility" IS NULL OR "hReversibility" BETWEEN 1 AND 5);

content.text:
I reviewed all the source, ran `pnpm install`, `tsc`, `eslint`, `pnpm audit` and a full `next build`, and checked a few suspicions directly. I haven't run the app against a live Postgres or in a browser, so the runtime items below come from reading the code. I made no changes to tracked files.

## Fix before shipping

**1. The documented default `JWT_SECRET` is a public secret that passes validation.**
- The README says to fill in `.env.example` "or keep the defaults". Its value, `change-me-to-a-long-random-string`, is 33 characters, so it passes the `< 16` check in `src/lib/auth.ts:9`.
- Anyone who deploys with the default can have session tokens forged by anyone who has read the repo. A forged token only needs a victim's user id as `sub`.
- Fix: reject placeholder values, and require at least 32 random bytes in production. Validate at boot rather than per request. Today a missing secret throws inside `proxy.ts` on every `/ideas` request, so users get a 500.

**2. There is no brute-force or abuse protection on auth.**
- `/api/auth/login` and `/register` have no rate limiting or lockout.
- Each hash uses pure-JS `bcryptjs` at cost 12, which took about 400 ms of CPU per hash here. An unauthenticated caller can pin the server with register or login requests.
- Fix: rate-limit per IP and per account, and consider native `bcrypt` or argon2.

**3. Existing accounts can be detected.**
- Register returns a distinct 409 "account already exists" (`register/route.ts:21`).
- Login returns early with no bcrypt work when the user doesn't exist (`login/route.ts:20`), so response timing also reveals which emails are registered.
- Fix: compare against a dummy hash when the user is missing. Decide whether the 409 is acceptable for this product.

**4. Passwords longer than 72 bytes are silently truncated.**
- `passwordSchema` allows up to 200 characters, but bcrypt only uses the first 72 bytes. I confirmed a 72-byte password and the same password plus a different suffix both verify against one hash.
- Fix: cap at 72 bytes, or pre-hash.

**5. There is no production migration path.**
- The only migration script is `prisma migrate dev`, which is dev-only. There is no `migrate deploy` step, Dockerfile or CI.
- The README's deploy story is `pnpm dev`, or `build && start` with no database step.

**6. Sessions can't be revoked.**
- Logout only clears the cookie. The JWT stays valid for 30 days, and there is no server-side session or version check.
- There is also no password reset, email verification, password change or account deletion. Password change and reset are what would let users invalidate stolen tokens. Deletion and export matter if you hold real users' data.

**7. Zero tests and no CI.**
- The only commit is "raw generated build, unreviewed", and there is no `test` script.
- Highest-value tests: ownership checks on every `[id]` route, share-token revoke and rotate, and score validation.

## Should fix

**8. Prediction scores can be edited after the outcome is recorded.**
- `PATCH /api/ideas/[id]` accepts `differentiation`, `evidence`, `cost` and `reversibility` at any time, and keeps no history.
- That undermines the point of the app, which is comparing what you predicted with what happened. Decide whether predictions should lock once an outcome exists.

**9. `PATCH` accepts inconsistent states.**
- `ideaUpdateSchema` allows setting `status` to `DONE` or `ABANDONED` with no outcome or hindsight scores.
- It also allows setting it back to `ACTIVE` while the old outcome and hindsight scores remain. Calibration keys off `hindsightTotal != null`, not status, so such ideas still count.
- Fix: drop `status` from the generic update, or enforce the invariants.

**10. Ownership checks are separate from the writes.**
- Every route does `findFirst({id, userId})` and then `update/delete({where:{id}})`. It's safe today, but a concurrent delete gives an unhandled P2025 500, and one refactor could drop the check.
- Fix: use `updateMany` or `deleteMany` with `{id, userId}`.

**11. Registration has a race.**
- `findUnique` then `create` means two concurrent signups hit the unique constraint (P2002) and return an unhandled 500. Catch the error and return 409.
- No route wraps Prisma calls in try/catch, so any DB error is an opaque 500 with no logging.

**12. There are no security headers.**
- `next.config.ts` is empty, so there is no CSP, HSTS, `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`, `Referrer-Policy` or `poweredByHeader: false`.
- The share page also has no `robots: noindex`, and its token sits in the URL. An "unlisted" link posted publicly can be indexed.

**13. Client error handling is thin.**
- Every `fetch` in the forms lacks try/catch, so on a network failure the button stays stuck on "Saving…" with no message.
- Delete (`idea-detail.tsx:79`) and all share-control actions fail silently. `navigator.clipboard` rejections are unhandled.

**14. Sharing exposes more than the UI says.**
- The `/s/[token]` page and `/api/share/[token]` include the outcome text and hindsight scores. The UI says only "anyone with the link can view this idea".
- Make that explicit, or add an option to share predictions only.

## Worth investigating or low priority

## Fix before shipping

**1. The documented default `JWT_SECRET` is a public secret that passes validation.**
- The README says to fill in `.env.example` "or keep the defaults". Its value, `change-me-to-a-long-random-string`, is 33 characters, so it passes the `< 16` check in `src/lib/auth.ts:9`.
- Anyone who deploys with the default can have session tokens forged by anyone who has read the repo. A forged token only needs a victim's user id as `sub`.
- Fix: reject placeholder values, and require at least 32 random bytes in production. Validate at boot rather than per request. Today a missing secret throws inside `proxy.ts` on every `/ideas` request, so users get a 500.

**2. There is no brute-force or abuse protection on auth.**
- `/api/auth/login` and `/register` have no rate limiting or lockout.
- Each hash uses pure-JS `bcryptjs` at cost 12, which took about 400 ms of CPU per hash here. An unauthenticated caller can pin the server with register or login requests.
- Fix: rate-limit per IP and per account, and consider native `bcrypt` or argon2.

**3. Existing accounts can be detected.**
- Register returns a distinct 409 "account already exists" (`register/route.ts:21`).
- Login returns early with no bcrypt work when the user doesn't exist (`login/route.ts:20`), so response timing also reveals which emails are registered.
- Fix: compare against a dummy hash when the user is missing. Decide whether the 409 is acceptable for this product.

**4. Passwords longer than 72 bytes are silently truncated.**
- `passwordSchema` allows up to 200 characters, but bcrypt only uses the first 72 bytes. I confirmed a 72-byte password and the same password plus a different suffix both verify against one hash.
- Fix: cap at 72 bytes, or pre-hash.

**5. There is no production migration path.**
- The only migration script is `prisma migrate dev`, which is dev-only. There is no `migrate deploy` step, Dockerfile or CI.
- The README's deploy story is `pnpm dev`, or `build && start` with no database step.

**6. Sessions can't be revoked.**
- Logout only clears the cookie. The JWT stays valid for 30 days, and there is no server-side session or version check.
- There is also no password reset, email verification, password change or account deletion. Password change and reset are what would let users invalidate stolen tokens. Deletion and export matter if you hold real users' data.

**7. Zero tests and no CI.**
- The only commit is "raw generated build, unreviewed", and there is no `test` script.
- Highest-value tests: ownership checks on every `[id]` route, share-token revoke and rotate, and score validation.

## Should fix

**8. Prediction scores can be edited after the outcome is recorded.**
- `PATCH /api/ideas/[id]` accepts `differentiation`, `evidence`, `cost` and `reversibility` at any time, and keeps no history.
- That undermines the point of the app, which is comparing what you predicted with what happened. Decide whether predictions should lock once an outcome exists.

**9. `PATCH` accepts inconsistent states.**
- `ideaUpdateSchema` allows setting `status` to `DONE` or `ABANDONED` with no outcome or hindsight scores.
- It also allows setting it back to `ACTIVE` while the old outcome and hindsight scores remain. Calibration keys off `hindsightTotal != null`, not status, so such ideas still count.
- Fix: drop `status` from the generic update, or enforce the invariants.

**10. Ownership checks are separate from the writes.**
- Every route does `findFirst({id, userId})` and then `update/delete({where:{id}})`. It's safe today, but a concurrent delete gives an unhandled P2025 500, and one refactor could drop the check.
- Fix: use `updateMany` or `deleteMany` with `{id, userId}`.

**11. Registration has a race.**
- `findUnique` then `create` means two concurrent signups hit the unique constraint (P2002) and return an unhandled 500. Catch the error and return 409.
- No route wraps Prisma calls in try/catch, so any DB error is an opaque 500 with no logging.

**12. There are no security headers.**
- `next.config.ts` is empty, so there is no CSP, HSTS, `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`, `Referrer-Policy` or `poweredByHeader: false`.

**13. Client error handling is thin.**
- Every `fetch` in the forms lacks try/catch, so on a network failure the button stays stuck on "Saving…" with no message.
- Delete (`idea-detail.tsx:79`) and all share-control actions fail silently. `navigator.clipboard` rejections are unhandled.

**14. Sharing exposes more than the UI says.**
- The `/s/[token]` page and `/api/share/[token]` include the outcome text and hindsight scores. The UI says only "anyone with the link can view this idea".
